tools.name: agent_os_task_create
tools.description: Create an AgentTask on the board. New tasks start `ready` (dispatchable now) unless you defer them: pass scheduledFor for a timed start (→ `scheduled`) or dependsOnTaskIds to gate on upstream work (→ `waiting`); both auto-promote to `ready` when their gate clears. Idempotent within the AgentOS: pass idempotencyKey (or requestId) from the foreground turn so a Telegram retry or Ghost restart returns the existing task instead of spawning a duplicate. Response includes `created` (false = an existing task was returned). Harness implementation slices whose titles begin Implement, Resume, Continue, or Finish require parentTaskId even when planId is present; create or reuse a feature parent first. Do NOT create closeout-only bookkeeping tasks whose purpose is merely to close/reconcile/clean up another task — complete/update/block/cancel the existing task (or spawn a child only for genuine unresolved implementation work).

title.description: Short task title (required). Never a closeout-only sweep — mutate/close the existing task instead.

priority.description: Priority is a worker-capacity queue signal, not importance. Default 'normal' (cleanup 'low'). Do NOT inherit plan/goal priority. Use 'high' only when harness workers are saturated and ready work waits for slots. Use 'critical' only for live production/security incidents — pass priorityEscalationReason or cite in title/description. When slots are free, omit priority and dispatch at normal. The API downgrades importance-style high/critical.

priorityEscalationReason.description: Required for critical: quote the requesting user or name the live production/security incident. High does not use this field — high requires worker-capacity contention at create time.

executor.description: How the task runs: inline | harness | acp | manual.

executorRef.description: Opaque ref to the executor process / unit.

parentTaskId.description: Feature-parent task id. Required for harness implementation slices whose title begins Implement, Resume, Continue, or Finish, including plan-linked slices.

planId.description: AgentPlan id to link this task to; required for plan-scoped harness work. This does not replace parentTaskId for implementation slices.

planStageId.description: Optional AgentPlan stage id for finer plan lineage.

personaSlug.description: Lane-expert worker slug to attribute the task to, or null to clear/filter unassigned tasks.

scheduledFor.description: ISO-8601 timestamp to defer the task to. A future time creates the task as `scheduled`; the operator loop auto-promotes it to `ready` once the time passes. null clears the schedule.

dependsOnTaskIds.description: Upstream task ids this task waits on. Creates the task as `waiting`; the operator loop auto-promotes it to `ready` once every listed task is `done` (a failed/cancelled upstream keeps it waiting).

standaloneReason.description: Required when intentionally creating an unscoped harness task without parentTaskId or planId; explain why it is standalone.

idempotencyKey.description: Dedupe key from the foreground turn. Strongly recommended.

requestId.description: Raw foreground request id; used as the dedupe key if idempotencyKey is absent.

tools.name: agent_os_ask_human
tools.description: Surface one decision to the human via the Action Required inbox. Each call MUST contain exactly one question the human can answer in one breath. Compound asks ('Do X? Or Y?') are rejected server-side with multiple_questions_detected — split them into two calls. Recommendation is required for category=decision|approval; supply the best-guess answer the user can one-tap accept. Returns the created `item` (with id you can pass to agent_os_await_action) and a `created` flag (false = idempotent re-create).

title.description: Short human headline for the owner's Home and Inbox card: what it is, in plain words (≤60 chars; no ids, file paths, SHAs or PR numbers).

question.description: The single question (one '?'). The user sees this verbatim.

body.description: Expanded context / background. Collapsed in the UI; expand-on-tap.

askerRef.description: Free-form ref (e.g. agent slug, reviewer id).

value.description: The recommended answer the user can accept with one tap.

taskId.description: Linked AgentTask id — unblocks on answer.

expiresAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp for hard deadline. Defaults to 24h for approvals; null otherwise.

clientRequestId.description: Dedupe key — repeating the same id within a user returns the existing item with created=false.

tools.name: agent_os_await_action
tools.description: Poll one Action Required item until it resolves. Returns immediately if the item is already terminal (answered / resolved_noop / expired / superseded / cancelled). If still open/snoozed, waits up to `timeoutSeconds` (default 60, max 300) with `pollIntervalSeconds` between checks. On answer, the answer text + acceptedRecommendation flag are returned so you can resume work without re-fetching.

itemId.description: The Action Required item id returned by agent_os_ask_human.

tools.name: agent_os_graph_query
tools.description: Read the operational graph's computed insights for the AgentOS: top bottlenecks (highest downstream impact among still-active or blocked work), per-owner load (who is carrying work and who is blocked), and orphaned tasks. Use this to answer questions like 'what is my biggest bottleneck', 'what is blocking project X', 'what is <persona> working on', or 'what is unassigned'. Read-only — modifies nothing. Returns { available, generatedAt, stats, insights }.

slug.description: AgentOS slug. Defaults to the configured env/primary AgentOS.

owners.description: Max per-owner load rows to return (default 12).

tools.name: agent_os_graph_view
tools.description: Steer the human's open 3D web view (shared focus) — spotlight + fly the camera to a node, a SET of nodes, or a whole goal constellation, filter, or reset, so you and the user are provably looking at the same thing while you narrate. kind=focus spotlights the target(s) and DIMS the rest (isolate); kind=highlight spotlights WITHOUT dimming. Give exactly one of: nodeId (a single node, e.g. 'task:abc'), nodeIds (an explicit set — 'frame these three bottlenecks'), or clusterId (the BARE goalId, NOT the 'goal:abc' node id — 'frame this whole goal'). An unrecognized target is dropped silently. frameAll=false keeps the camera put (spotlight only, no fly). kind=filter sets which type/status buckets are hidden; kind=reset clears focus + filters + spotlight. Takes effect only while the user has the 3D Web tab open (delivered over SSE). Requires Redis in multi-instance/serverless prod to fan out; single-instance dev works without it.

slug.description: AgentOS slug. Defaults to env/primary.

kind.description: focus (spotlight + dim rest) | highlight (spotlight, no dim) | filter | reset.

nodeId.description: focus/highlight: a single target node id (e.g. 'task:abc123').

nodeIds.description: focus/highlight: an explicit SET of node ids to frame together.

clusterId.description: focus/highlight: a whole goal constellation = the BARE goalId (the Goal entity id, e.g. 'abc'; the value in each node's web3d.constellation.goalId), NOT the prefixed 'goal:abc' graph node id. An unknown id resolves to nothing (no-op).

frameAll.description: focus/highlight: also fly the camera to frame the set (default true).

hiddenKinds.description: For kind=filter: node kinds to hide (e.g. ['repo_file']). [] clears.

hiddenStatuses.description: For kind=filter: statuses to hide (e.g. ['done']). [] clears.

Default projection=compact returns a tiny navigable brief (<12k UTF-8): heads-up counts, capped running tasks, top next actions/blockers, and follow-up tool hints. Deep detail requires agent_os_task_get, agent_os_plan_get, agent_os_tasks_list, or graph tools. Pass projection=full only for admin/debug (expensive, truncation-prone browser rollup). Same aggregate as the browser Command Center. Omit slug to use env/primary workspace; pass agentOsId when already known from a prior identity fetch.

Supports idempotency via idempotencyKey. signal: 'positive' for helpful retrievals or correct outcomes, 'negative' for misses or corrections. outcomeKind: one of retrieval_used | retrieval_miss | human_correction | task_review_pass | task_review_fail | pr_linked | eval_example | regression_failure.

idempotencyKey.description: Unique key to prevent duplicate records for the same event.

slug.description: AgentOS slug. Defaults to configured primary.

tools.description: Set why a human_correction event happened. Only memory_wrong counts against L1 memory health. requirement_change: the owner changed an instruction (old memory was right when written). memory_wrong: the stored fact was false or stale. test: self-test traffic. unclassified removes the label. Changes are appended to the event's history, so relabeling reverts. Operator access required (owner or admin).

slug.description: AgentOS slug. Defaults to configured primary.

feedbackId.description: id of the human_correction feedback event.

note.description: Short audit note (no private memory content).

tools.name: agent_os_memory_quality_l1_health_get
tools.description: Fetch compact authoritative L1 memory-quality health for cron and reporting consumers. Returns L1-filtered counts, score/health, highlights, and excluded review-pipeline noise. Only memory_wrong corrections are scored; `corrections` splits every correction by reason (requirement_change, test, unclassified). health=insufficient_data means too few L1 signals for a verdict. Operator access required (owner or admin). Read-only.

slug.description: AgentOS slug. Defaults to configured primary.

windowHours.description: Rolling health window in hours. Defaults to 24; maximum 720.

tools.name: agent_os_memory_quality_status_get
tools.description: List recent memory quality feedback events for the AgentOS workspace. Operator access required (owner or admin). Supports filtering by signal (positive|negative), outcomeKind, and a time window via 'since'. Returns items array and count. With 'since', also returns the same `corrections` breakdown as l1-health and tags each human_correction item with correctionReasonClass and correctionCluster (duplicates share a cluster). Pair with agent_os_command_center_get to see the memoryQuality rollup (aggregate counts + regression gate status).

slug.description: AgentOS slug. Defaults to the configured env/primary AgentOS.

outcomeKind.description: Filter to a specific outcome kind.

since.description: ISO timestamp — only include events recorded after this instant.

limit.description: Max events to return (server default 50, max 500).

tools.name: agent_os_memory_candidates_list
tools.description: List memory suggestions (promotion candidates) for the AgentOS workspace with their triage state and queue counts. Operator access required (owner or admin). Read-only. needsHuman=true returns only the short human digest: suggestions no rule or small model could settle, oldest first. autoClosed=true returns suggestions closed automatically (reversible via decide reopen). Each item carries `kind`, `ageDays` and `triage` ({tier, action, rule, reason, confidence, duplicateCount}). `counts` reports pending, needsHuman, untriagedPending, autoClosed, approved, rejectedByHuman, rolledBack.

slug.description: AgentOS slug. Defaults to the configured env/primary AgentOS.

needsHuman.description: Only items waiting on a human decision (the digest).

autoClosed.description: Only items closed automatically by triage.

tools.name: agent_os_memory_candidates_decide
tools.description: Decide on memory suggestions in batch (up to 50 ids per call) with a one-line reason. approve: apply the suggestion through the reviewed promotion path. reject: close it (audited). merge: fold the listed suggestions into `mergeInto` (they close with a pointer to it). reopen: bring a suggestion that triage closed automatically back into the queue. Operator access required (owner or admin). Each id reports ok/error independently; nothing is deleted.

slug.description: AgentOS slug. Defaults to configured primary.

reason.description: One-line reason recorded on the audit event.

tools.name: agent_os_memory_candidates_triage_run
tools.description: Run memory-suggestion triage for the workspace: rules first (no model), then a small model on what is left, leaving only genuinely uncertain items for a human. DRY RUN BY DEFAULT — the report shows what each step would close, bank as an eval example, fold into a duplicate, or hand to a human, and writes nothing. Pass dryRun=false to apply. tier1=false runs rules only. The daily small-model cost cap is enforced server-side. Operator access required (owner or admin). Never deletes anything; closes are reversible.

slug.description: AgentOS slug. Defaults to configured primary.

tier1.description: Default true. false skips the small-model step.

limit.description: Pending rows to consider, oldest first (default 500).

tools.name: agent_os_operating_rules_get
tools.description: Return the workspace's standing agent instruction policy. Returns operating rules by exact lookup, not semantic search. Operator access required; internal-tier mechanics visible to Kynver platform admins only. Set includeMarkdown=1 to receive prompt injection text. Standing rules load by topic: pass `text` (the user's latest message, plus `quote` for a replied-to message) to get exactly the rules that turn needs — the every-turn rules plus every rule of the topics the message mentions (deterministic word match, full text). Pass topicOverview=true for rules grouped by topic, the every-turn cap and rules still waiting for a topic.

slug.description: AgentOS slug (defaults from env / primary).

personaSlug.description: Worker persona slug for additive persona rules.

planId.description: Optional plan id for envelope context.

includeMarkdown.description: When true, include formatted markdown suitable for worker prompts.

text.description: A message: returns the standing rules that would load for it (always + matched topics).

quote.description: The message being replied to, matched with `text`.

topics.description: Topic slugs to load regardless of the message text.

topicOverview.description: When true, return rules grouped by topic with token use, the every-turn cap and rules waiting for a topic.

tools.name: agent_os_operating_rule_set
tools.description: Promote one saved memory to a standing rule, or retire one back to an ordinary memory. Standing rules load by topic: a new rule is filed under the workspace topics its words match (load "topic"), or waits for the owner to pick one (load "needs-topic") — pass `topics` to choose. load "always" (every turn) is for a tiny floor only and is refused when the every-turn rules would pass their token cap; then give it a topic. Identify the memory by key or memoryId. Idempotent; retiring keeps the memory. Operator access required. Returns the rule's load/topics and the refreshed status; if status.topicLoading shows rules waiting for a topic, tell the user.

slug.description: AgentOS slug (defaults from env / primary).

key.description: Memory key (slug). One of key or memoryId is required.

memoryId.description: Memory id. One of key or memoryId is required.

action.description: promote = make it a standing rule; retire = stop loading it (memory is kept).

category.description: Rule category (promote only; inferred when omitted).

scope.description: invariant = never overridden by persona rules; overridable (default) otherwise.

load.description: How the rule loads (promote only). Omit to auto-assign topics from the rule's words.

topics.description: Topic slugs from the workspace's topic list (promote only; implies load "topic").

Load a section with agent_os_get_skill_section and a file with agent_os_get_skill_file only when the core points you to it. Owner-only write: only call when the workspace owner asked for this decision.

tools.name: agent_os_memory_ledger_summary
tools.description: Read a narrated summary of the workspace owner's signed memory access ledger (receipt counts, recent human-framed activity lines, chain integrity, and workbench steering hints). Use when the operator asks what memories were read, what changed, or wants a weekly digest. Customer vocabulary only — no retrieval mechanics. After summarizing, offer to open Memory activity via agent_os_workbench_view (kind=open_panel, panel=memory-activity). Read-only and safe for unattended use.

tools.name: agent_os_limitation_check

Pass a short subject (e.g. 'kariad facebook reel ai label') or the exact sentence you were about to repeat. Returns status: open (a recorded blocker whose fix hasn't shipped), fixed (its linked fix PR merged and deployed — do NOT report it as a blocker), or unverified (no recorded blocker, or one with no linked fix older than 3 days — recheck the live system first). Also returns fixedBy/fixedAt, evidence and the matching memory keys.

subject.description: Short subject of the limitation, in plain words.

tools.name: agent_os_limitation_sweep
tools.description: Retire limitation (blocker) memories whose linked fix has shipped (merged + deployed). Operator access required. Normally runs on its own every few minutes; use after merging a fix to retire its blocker immediately.

slug.description: Workspace slug. Omit for your own primary workspace.

tools.name: agent_os_macro_controls_get
tools.description:
Fetch the current macro/social trend snapshot so you can adapt marketing content to active signals.

WHEN TO CALL: before generating social media posts, ad copy, campaign briefs, launch announcements,
trend-reactive content, or any marketing material where current events could affect brand perception.
This is an on-demand catch-up step — call it at the START of social/content/marketing work, not on
every message.

WHAT YOU GET: a compact MacroControlSnapshot with active MacroTrendSignals (topic, sensitivity,
summary, confidence, sourceLinks), a globalSensitivity aggregate ('safe'|'cautious'|'sensitive'|'blocked'),
isStale flag, and agentGuidance text you should incorporate into your content plan.

GATING RULES:
- globalSensitivity='blocked': do NOT publish related content — surface the blocked topics to the
  operator and wait for explicit approval before proceeding.
- globalSensitivity='sensitive': draft with extra care, avoid direct references to flagged topics,
  prefer evergreen angles, and flag for human review before posting.
- globalSensitivity='cautious': note flagged topics in your plan; adjust tone but may proceed.
- globalSensitivity='safe' or isStale=true with no signals: proceed with standard brand voice.

If isStale=true AND signals are present, treat the data as advisory only and note staleness in your
output so the operator knows to refresh. Read-only; safe for unattended invocation.

tools.name: agent_os_focus_get
tools.description: Get the current agent-loop focus and active executor leases for this AgentOS workspace. Returns two separate buckets:   agentLoopFocus   — plan rows currently marked `in_progress` (agent/Hermes focus, NOT executor state).   executorLeases   — tasks with status `running` and an active worker lease. Never conflate the two: in_progress = current-focus intent; running = live executor heartbeat. Pass todos=true to also receive a projected Hermes-like todo list.

todos.description: When true, also return a projected todo list of actionable tasks and in-progress rows.

planId.description: Scope the todo projection to a single plan. Has no effect unless todos=true.

slug.description: AgentOS workspace slug. Omit to use env or the server-discovered primary.

tools.name: agent_os_focus_set
tools.description: Set the agent-loop current focus to a specific plan progress row. This marks the row as `in_progress` and updates AgentPlan.inProgressRowKey. IMPORTANT: This does NOT set the task status to `running` — that is the executor lease. Hermes `in_progress` semantics: focus intent, not worker heartbeat. Other in_progress rows on the plan stay in progress (several rows may be in progress at once, one per parallel worker); only the plan's focus pointer moves. Precondition: the plan must have focus enabled (progressFocusEnabled not set to false in plan metadata). When focus is disabled, returns applied:false with a reason — not an error, but the change was not applied.

planId.description: The plan that owns the row to focus.

rowKey.description: Progress row key to focus. One of rowKey or rowId is required.

rowId.description: Progress row DB id to focus. One of rowKey or rowId is required.

taskId.description: Associate a task with this focus event (metadata only — does not change task status).

roleLane.description: Role lane making this focus change. Defaults to implementer.

note.description: Optional note recorded on the focus event.

slug.description: AgentOS workspace slug. Omit to use env or the server-discovered primary.

tools.name: agent_os_focus_clear
tools.description: Clear the agent-loop current focus for a plan, moving the focused row back to `todo`. Use when the session is done with a row but not marking it complete. Does NOT cancel or abort the associated task — task lifecycle is separate.

planId.description: The plan whose current focus should be cleared.

roleLane.description: Role lane making this focus change. Defaults to implementer.

note.description: Optional note recorded on the clear event.

slug.description: AgentOS workspace slug. Omit to use env or the server-discovered primary.

tools.name: agent_os_todo_project
tools.description: Project the current AgentOS task board and plan progress rows into a Hermes-like todo list. Returns KynverTodoItem entries with origin discriminants:   plan_row      — an in_progress plan progress row (agent-loop focus).   task_ready    — a task ready for dispatch.   task_blocked  — a task blocked on external input.   task_needs_input — a task waiting on human decision. Includes stale detection: items not updated within 48h are flagged stale=true. Use this as the authoritative 'what is next' readback for Kynver sessions, replacing stale Hermes-local todos with live board state.

planId.description: Scope to a single plan. Omit for workspace-wide projection.

slug.description: AgentOS workspace slug. Omit to use env or the server-discovered primary.
